messages.text: Do Not Use
Nothing seems to happen.

A genuine thirst ravages your aching bodies.  Days of travel without water have made you weak and in need of shelter.  A vast, mountainous wall around you and only one direction to walk.  Enjoy Twin Sands of Time!
Ahead of you steaming pools of water are intermixed with odd looking trees and shrubs of all types.  The water is highly acidic and not sufficient to drink.
One of the water holes you discover contains pure, clean water.  You eagerly replenish your supplies.
Some creepy slime things slurp out of the water pits and attack.
The water has a cleansing effect.  The magical pool has some special properties.
But wait.  You detect a magical aura coming from the pool!  You cannot distinguish what it is, but its definately magical.  Will you replenish your supplies?
The crew bails out and continues the fight!!!
Across your path you notice a crude trip wire.  The wire goes into the stone wall connected to who knows what.  Would you like to disarm it or simply avoid it?
Disarm Trap
Avoid Trap
Who will attampt this?
Trip wire!  Your clumsiness has tripped a trip wire.  A hail of arrows greets you head on, as well as calls undue attention to yourselves.
Success....  You carefully cut the trip wire and place it gingerly on the floor, not setting off any traps or calling undue attention to yourselves.
You cut the trip wire in an attempt to disarm the trap...

...that strange sound doesn't bode well for your health.  A hail of arrows comes from both sides of the corridor and into your party.  The commotion has for sure notified the inhabitants of this dungeon as to your arrival.
A group of eight Ogres stand guard here.  They are surprised at your entrance.  They gather themselves quickly though and attack.
Not much left to scrounge for but a few coins.
In a well-timed ambush eight ogres toss boulders upon you followed by a surprise attack!  They were waiting for you.
A set of stairs is revealed behind the door.  Would you like to follow them up?
A stairs leads down.  Follow them?
More ogre guards join the fight!
This barracks lie empty.  The inhabitants, it seems, left in a hurry.
A large contingent of ogres are assembled here, all milling about very casually.  You surprise them.  They run about in an effort to become organized, but is not very effective.
The main gate to the city of Arl.  The gates are locked.  From a nearby tower you hear a guard yell, "Who goes there?  What is your business here?"  What is your answer?
As you turn and leave the guards resume their normal activities pacing about in the towers above.
"The town of Arl is not in the habit of charity.  To enter costs 20 gold.  Toss it over the gate and you will be granted entrance."
Do you toss over the money?
A quick inventory of your treasure indicates you don't have enough gold to toss over the fence.
You toss the gold over.  A guard scurries down the tower, scoops up the gold and opens the gate.  You enter.  The guard shuts the gate behind you.

"Adventure, ey?  Plenty of adventures in these parts.  C'mon in.  See the mercenary guild for an assignment."  A guard scurries down and opens the gate.  You enter.  The guard shuts the gate behind you.
"Ahhhh....  looking to spend some gold on our merchants.  Welcome."  A guard scurries down and opens the gate.  You enter.  The guard shuts the gate behind you.
The huge iron gate swings open and slams and locks behind you.
A sign tacked above the door reads "Mercenary Guild."  Would you like to enter?
A small but effective temple.  A cleric greets you wearing flowing reddish- maroon robes.  Prices are a bit steep.
The local bank.  A man greets you.  "Good day.  Would you like to open an account with us?"

"Good.  Please, sit down.  Now.  Here are the forms you must fill out in order to bank with us.  We offer storage of all of your valuables.  Just fill these out and you will be set.  All done?  Good.  Now, just sign here and you are all set."
"Every time you access your account it costs you 50 gold."  Do you sign the forms to open your account?

The man returns with a key.  "Good.  This is the key to your storage room.  You can store your money and valuables there.  Just remember, everytime you access your storage it costs you 50 gold.  Thanks for your business and have a nice day."
"Welcome.  Would you like to access your account and pay me 50 gold?"
Thank you.  You may access your storage room.
Sorry.  You don't have the proper funds.  Come back when you do."
A small sign depicts this as the local weapon smithy.  Do you enter the shop?
A small sign depicts this as the local armor smithy.  Do you enter the shop?
A small sign depicts this as the local supply store.  Do you enter the shop?
Made of gleaming silver, these torches illuminate, even in daylight, the surrounding countryside.
A small, plain sign reads, "The Stow-Away."  Do you enter?
Would you like to exit?
A wooden door sits slightly open.  The voices of people can be heard inside.
A huge ornate rug cobers the vast room before you.  Across the room are two desks and a man dressed in a blue robe.  He hails you, "Welcome!  Come on over!"
Under the rug you discover a hidden trap door.  Would you like to move the rug and open the trap door?

The man in blue robes across the room yells to you, "Hey.... do you often lift up peoples rugs and look underneath them?"  He looks over his shoulder as if to get someone's attention.  Do you continue opening the trap door?
"Stop.  Stop now!"  The man in blue yells in your direction but you continue your examination of the trap door.

Your ignoring of the man has brought some attention on yourselves.  A group of  town guards rushes into the room.  The leader speaks, "Stop now and leave the inn at once or we will be forced to take action against you."  Do you listen?
They attack as promised.
You clear away the rug and reveal the trap door.
Would you like to enter?
Having defeated the guards the trap door is left unattended.
The guards roughly remove you from the inn.  "Do not return here again.  We do not want your business!"  He slams the door.
A small, plain sign reads, "The Stow-Away."  A man in blue robes looks out the window and double bolts the door upon seeing you.

The man in blue robes speaks, "Welcome to the Stow-Away.  I am Kral.  Host of this fine establishment.  Finest food in the land.  Along with the drink.  And the beds.  Anyway, will you be staying with us?
The door is locked.
The lock springs open!  You slip inside.
The lock holds.
You succesfully circumnavigate the door and get to the other side.  Your party joins you.
A lovely woman in a red dress answers the door.  She states, "The host will get you your room.  This is private storage for our guests.  Thank you."  She begins to close the door.  What do you do?
A lady in a red dress yells to you, "Hey!  This is a private stock room!  Leave at once!"  Do you leave?
"Thats okay.  Enjoy your visit.  The restaurant is to the south.  Thank you and have a fine day."  He seems way too happy.

"Great!  The rates are 10 gold/week.  We will need 10 gold to start and we will have someone dispatched to collect 10 gold from you every week until you check out.  Please sign here."  Do you sign and pay the ten gold?
I'd love to give you a room if you had the gold!"  Please enjoy your visit and come back when you are equipped to pay for it."
"Super!  You are in room 3-A.  Take your key and enjoy your stay.  Thank you soooo much."  He hands you your iron room key.
Kral is so friendly.  "Hello.  So nice to see you.  I hope your stay is just super!"
Out of the thin air an apparition appears.  "I am sent by Kral.  Please pay me 10 gold to upkeep your room."  Do you pay?
"Thank you!  Have a nice day."  The apparition fades.
"If you do not pay, you do not get your room.  Do you pay?"
"You do not have enough money.  You lose your room.  Have a nice day.  Kral will be very upset."  Your iron room key vanishes, as does the apparition.
"That is your option.  Thank you for staying with us."  Your iron key vanishes, as does the apparition.
"Oh, excuse me....I'll get out of your way."  Kral exits out the door.
Glancing at the extremely neat desk you get a sense that a secret drawer exists in it.  Care to investigate?
Glancing at the papers on the desk you don't see anything of significance.

There is a drawer.  There is a guest manifest inside.  The manifest is a list of names and how much each has paid for their stay here and whether or not they are keeping anything in the special storage area available to all guests.

It reads:   3-A:  Empty.  3-B :  Mr. & Mrs. Sclube, 50/wk, valuables in storage.  3-C:  Horak Grawan, 150/wk, valuable in storage.  3-D:  Count Vorchaz, 350/wk, something in storage (Would not give info).  3-E:  Not prepared/closed.
Kral looks at you.  "Excuse me, those are my private papers.  Do you mind?"  He shoos you away.
You slip your key into the door and open the lock.
The door is locked.  What would you like to do?
No one answers the door.  It remains locked.
The door has a room number on it: 3-B.  It is locked.
The door has a room number on it: 3-A.
The key slides in and unlocks the door.
The door has a room number on it:  3-C.
You slip out the door.  It locks behind you.
You slip out the door.  It locks behind you.  You have mastered this lock.  You may slip in and out undetected.
A very messy desk indeed.  Nothing of interest there.
The door closes and locks behind you.
The door has a room number on it:  3-D.  It is locked.
The door has a room number on it:  3-E.  It is locked.
As soon as you set foot in the door a voice booms, "Halt!  Stop where you are.  Surrender your weapons and come peaceably.  How dare you break in the room of Count Vorchaz."
A very large man and a smaller one approach you with weapons drawn.  They are ready to strike if you do not surrender.  Do you surrender?
The two men quickly remove all of your wordly possessions, shackle you together,  and roughly take you downstairs.
You are dragged in front of Kral.  The larger guard speaks, "These men broke in the room of Count Vorchaz.  We do not pay 350gp/week for this type of service.  We demand justice."

You see Kral's face ashen considerably then turn beet red.  "I promise you sir.  I will see these men to justice.  They seemed upstanding when they arrived but I now know they are nothing but coniving thieves."

The two guards eye each other and seem satisfied. "You will remove 1 weeks pay from our bill for this outrage, understand Kral?"  Kral responds sheepishly, "Yes, sir.  It is done.  Thank you.  And thank the Count."

Kral turns to you, "What in the name of Hades do you think you were doing?  That cost me 350 gold!  Not to mention Count Vorchaz is gonna have my head when he gets word of this!  He's a bad man, that one!  Rules with a cold heart and a cold...
...piece of steel.  Thanks.  Now I have to haul your sorry hides down to the courthouse.  Lets go."  He takes you to the courthouse, flanked by 15 of the town guard.
The two men are on you quickly, gaining first strike!
The town guard arrives after hearing the commotion.
Having defeated the Count's guards you have roam of his room.
The chest is locked.
The lock breaks off in your hands.  You open the chest.
No effect.
Kral looks both directions and seeing the coast is clear begs you over.  Do you go to the window?

Kral speaks in hushed tones so no one may overhear him.  "I know I banned you from this place and I have your equipment.  But now I need your help.  This Count Vorchaz is something terrible.  I'm not sure what it is but I know he is...

...hiding some horrible secret.  Late at night I hear mumblings from his room followed by horrible muffled screams.  I cannot attract any more customers!  If you agree to find out his secret so I can get rid of him I will get you your...
...money and equipment.  Then, once I get rid of him as your reward you can have the items of his in the storage area.  Is it a deal?
"I understand.  If you change your mind I'll be here.  Good day."
"Good.  Here are your belongings and money.  Return here when you have found out something."  He slips out the back door and dumps a huge chest at your feet.  In it are your belongings and wealth.
Kral looks out the window.  He nods in your direction and you continue on.
The courthouse is currently empty.
Kral hauls you before justice Survd.  Sentencing is swift. "You are hereby fined 1500 gold.  If you cannot pay you will spend 45 days in the jail.  Who will pay the fine?"

"Well, since you do not have the money you will be spending 45 days in our lovely jail.  Bailiff...take them away."   Kral speaks up....."Wait.  I will pay their fine for them if you can guarantee me they will never be near my inn again."  The...

...justice looks confused.  "Why would you do this Kral?"  Kral answers, "One, I know our jail is probably certain death and they do not deserve that.  Two, even if they do jail time, they might be back.  This way I have a guarantee they will never come..

...to my place of business again.  If they do, then the jail time should be set at 45 years, not days.  Agreed?"  The Justice pauses for a time and then slowly nods... "Agreed Kral.  You pay the fine and these thieves will not bother you again."  The...

...Justice turns to you.  "Be warned.  45 years if you ever bother this man again.  Court is adjourned."  Kral pays your fine and quickly leaves.  You aren't sure how or if you'll ever get your stuff back.
The dresser contains many boring personal effects such as socks, shirts, and the like.  Under the socks is a piece of paper with the word "guardian" scribbled on it.
You make your retreat.
Your spell discovers a hidden drawer.  It is locked.
You are standing before the Count's dresser.
You successfully circumvent the lock.
You see a large, very sharp needle tipped with poison wedged into the lock.  You sucessfully extract and destroy it.
A large, very sharp needle tipped with poison wedged into the lock sticks into your hand.  You feel its results.
Who will do this?
Your search reveals nothing of interest.
Inside the drawere is a letter to Count Vorchaz.  It reads,  "Dear Count,  To date we have not received any news of the situation in Arl.  We await your response.  Respectfully yours,  Lord Florn.
Would you like to keep this letter?
A small gathering of huts is gathered in the dust of the desert.  A lone pillar of smoke rises from the chimney of a home in the north.

Smoke rises from the chimney of this small hut.  A young man walks out of the front door and greets you.  "Good day.  Ahhh, the fine smell of sand and sun.  Nothing beats that.  My name is Sha' Nar, feller of beasts.  I am in need of adventure.
I offer you my services.  I will be faithful to you and any quest in which we may encounter.  Do you wish me to join you?"
What would you like to do?
The creaky wooden gate opens easily at your touch.
You wander into the local tannery.  His wares are for sale.
A band of thugs is kicking around the town kitty.  Do you attempt to save it?
The thugs look at you and laugh, "Hah!  Try and stop our fun, will you?  I think not!"  They attack you as the kitty cowers in fear.
The kitty has taken a liking to you.  She won't leave you alone.  Do you keep her?
She climbs into your nearest knapsack and falls quickly asleep.  "Prrrrrrrrrr...."

As you approach the wooden gate a group of rag-tag guards runs up to you, "Halt!  Who is approaching Blun' dar?  State your names for the record and enter knowing crime and/or mischief is not allowed."  After doing so, you enter.
A group of hum drum guards are lodging here.  Some awake, some asleep, others in a total daze.  You enter, walk around and are not even noticed.  So, you leave.
A group of hum drum guards are lodging here.  Some drunk, some gambling, others in a total daze.  You enter, walk around and are not even noticed.  So, you leave.
A group of hum drum guards are lodging here. Some drooling, some sleeping, others in a total state of utter confusion.  You enter, walk around and are not even noticed.  So, you leave.

A group of hum drum guards are lodging here. Some seem drunk, others sleeping, two even dancing together in a sick display of affection.  You enter, walk around and are not even noticed.  So, you leave.

An old human woman runs out of her house, sniffing the air.  "I smell my kitty, precious.  Precious!  Precious!  Where are you?"  She is obviously blind as a skulk bat.  Do you relate how you rescued her precious, or keep quiet and move on?
Tell the story
Keep quiet/move on
The old woman follows you for a bit, always sniffing the air.  She gives up eventually, her nose lowered as tears fall from her blind eyes.

You relate the story of the daring rescue of precious.  She thanks you for rescuing her and for returning precious safely.  The old woman takes precious from you and tosses her on the porch.  She digs into her bosom and pulls out a broach.  "A token...
...of my gratitude."  You gladly accept it.
A band of orcs has invaded the village and attacks you.
An old lady sits on her porch rocking to and fro.  She is muttering to herself in some strange tongue when....
She transforms into an ostrich.  A few odd croakings later.....
...and she returns to the old lady rocking in the chair.
A group of orcs spots you and attacks.
Two beautiful rows of huge green trees belie the dryness of this desert.

A group of horses rides up to greet you.  The leader, dressed in red, greets you.  "Whoa, men.  You now enter the land of Allimac.  This is private land and you have no appointment or need to see her.  Be off now."  They escort you to the road.

Three men of tremendous girth greet you on the bridge.  The largest one speaks, "Whoa, men.  You now enter the land of Allimac.  This is private land and you have no appointment or need to see her.  Be off now."  They escort you to the road.
The orcs carried a map!
An empty house.
Your searching reveals some steps going down in what otherwise might be an empty house.  Would you like to take them down?
A stairway leads up.  Take it?
A patrol of orcs is searching the room.  They see you and attack.
Two ogres are busy here chewing on the leg of a long dead goblin.  They see you and get even more hungry!
A pair of Minotaurs are waiting for you.  They attack.
A whole bunch of zombies aimlessly patrol the room.  They sniff the air, pick up your scent and turn on you!
A hill giant stirs from his slumber as you clumsily open the door.  He attacks with suprise.
Some bizarre looking creatures slither toward you and attack.
This room is currently unoccupied.  Emphasis on currently.
A gaggle of undead sloth about the room.  They turn their attention to you.
A chest lies poorly hidden in the corner.  It appears unlocked.  Will you open it?
Who will open the chest?
You have detected a trap.  You quickly and easily remove the poison needle lodged in the hinge of the lid.  You open the chest.  It contains treasure.
A poison needle jabs into your hand doing serious damage.  You get the chest open and it reveals treasure.
A startled set of guards did not expect you.  The quickly gather themselves and attack.
More orcs come screaming down the hall on you!

A large stone table is in the center of this room.  A single sword hovers above the table.  Mages and clerics are trying to undue some sort of incantation of good which has been blessed upon this blade.  They see you enter the room and attack.

Having destroyed the evil clerics and wizards, you approach the sword.  It glows and hums with a great blue-white light.  As the last of the clerics breathes his last breath, the sword falls to the table, its evil spell broken.  You claim your prize.
A horde of giant frogs take refuge here.  You startle them and they attack.
The frogs have garnished some treasure.
A short, stocky man emerges from this humble abode.  "Come, come.  Buy my wares."  He beckons you inside.  Do you follow?
A young lady dressed in beautiful flowing silken white robes dabs tears from her eyes.  Do you approach her?

"I...I'm sorry to be cryin' like this, dear sirs.  I must say I am quite embarrassed.  My name is Kirina and I have lost my most sacred possession....my diary.  Without it I will not remember all of my wonderful....
...memories of my childhood.  I wish I could get it back.  I would do ANYTHING to get that back.  Do y'all think you could help?"
"Oh, that is wonderful.  Just come back here when you find it and I'll reward you all right."  With that she slinks back into her home and shuts the door.
Enable Kirina diary section.

Kirina comes out of the house, tears flowing down her cheek.  "My diary, my diary!  You have found my diary.  Thank you so much."  She quickly composes herself.  "Now, for your reward.  Who will join me in my home and claim the reward?"
Kirina looks about, "Ohhh, still no diary.  I guesss you will have to wait for your reward then."  She goes slinkily back into the house.
A family of giant centipedes has made a nest here.  They attack as though you are easy prey.
Would you like to search the nest?
You find little of value except a very unremarkable book.

You follow Kirina into her home.  She wheels to face you.  The door slams shut behind you.  As you watch, the once beautiful Kirina twists and contorts into a wretched Hag.  She attacks with a bellow!
Kirina emerges from her home as beautiful as ever, if not even a little flushed red in the cheeks.  "Who will be next to claim the reward?"  Does someone volunteer?
"Who will join me in my home and claim the reward?"
You destroy the hag!  Well done.  You find some items of interest in the home.  You grab what you want and return to your party.
"So, no one wants the reward!  I guess I'll have to give it to you right here!"  As you watch, the once beautiful Kirina twists and contorts into a wretched Hag.  She attacks with a bellow!
The door opens easily at your gentle push.
A townsman walks up to you and bids you good day.
A townsman walks past you with a kind "excuse me."
A lovely lady smiles at you as you pass.
A small child runs into your leg, but apologizes with a heart felt "I'm so sorry.  Please excuse me."
A young man in his teens passes you and greets you warmly.
A lady with a carriage walks bye and smiles cheerfully in your direction.
A puny dwarf squats behind a large oaken desk.  "Check the job board!," he barks.  Turning to your left you notice some job postings tacked to the wall.  Care to investigate?
Finding no job interesting, you leave.  "Come back when you get some courage," snaps the puny dwarf.

What a horrific sight!  Mobs of orcs terrorizing what once was a peaceful township.  Small groups of orcs are all about the village, attacking anyone in sight....men, women or children.  You know what you must do.  Do you join the fight?
The orcs finish off the villagers and come after you.  How cowardly you are!
The village is in ruins.  All the people are dead, all thier belongings taken off while you fought with the remaining orc force.  You have failed.
Brave indeed.  A milieu of bodies, both human and orc, engulf you.  The battle is joined.
More orcs join in the battle.

You have defeated the orc raiding party.  A bedragggled man approaches you, "I am Raolph.  Thank you for helping us.  But this occurs regularily.  We must find the orc lair and destroy all of them there in order to end this menace to my village."
"Will you help me?"
"I understand.  Thank you for your consideration."  Raolph leaves, knowing his fate.  You have failed to complete this quest.
"Very good.  We leave at once.  One of my men was able to 'convince' an orc raider to draw us this crude map.  The hide-out must be there somewhere.  Let's go!"
The dwarf grumbles, "Let's see here....okay...here's a map...that's all I got.  Good luck.  You keep what you get."
Whoa.....
The ground shudders beneath your feet as a huge hole opens up in the earth underfoot and swallows you.

Although you are uninjured, it takes a second to get your bearings back.  Raolph interjects, "I know it....this is the lair of the orcs.  I don't know why I know...I just know."  His eyes flare with determination.  You move on.
Although you are uninjured, it takes a second to get your bearings back.  You wish Raolph were here to help you out!
Raolph hesitates, then speaks, "Wait....we should go south...maybe...I'm not sure...."
Your searching reveals a trip wire.  You step over it easily and move on.
You clumsily trip a trip wire.  Spears shoot at you from the walls.
Stairs lead up.  Take them?
A gathering of orc magic users are here.  They spot yu and unleash their magic.
A patrol searches the room.  They spot you.
The patrol was carrying some treasure.

A single orc roams the room.  He spots you and drops his weapon.  In crude common he speaks, "Silly Humans...You will not defeat us.  EVER!!!!"  He pulls a long rope which was hiding in the shadows and an alarm goes off.
It will not be long before the orcs are on you.

A single orc roams the room.  He spots you and drops his weapon.  In crude common he speaks, "Silly Humans...You will not defeat us. Raolph?"  The orc looks strangely at Raolph then at you.  "Raolph...you, you should not have come here.

Raolph responds, "Tugloc?  I thought you agreed to start a new life, away from here?!"  "I did," Tugloc grunts, "until my son was taken by commander Grunk!  I'm here looking for him!"  Raolph ponders for a moment then explains what your.....

...intentions are here.  Tugloc pauses, "Okay, the commander is at the end of the hall.  My son is being kept north of here.  You go get the commander and I'll get my son.  I'll meet you back at the commander's chamber.  Agreed?"

"Agreed," Raolph responds.  Tugloc takes his hand away from an alarm rope in the shadows and heads past you.  Raolph turns to you, "Tugloc has a good heart.  One of the few orcs to ever see the evil in their way.  Let's go take out the commander!"
The alarm has brought a bunch of orcs upon your position.  They attack with vigor.
The majority of the orc contingent is wiped out.  One of the dying orcs grunts in common before he dies, "You will never get commander Grunk!  He knows you are coming"  He dies.
The room is currently empty.
Commander Grunk is here flanked by his champions.  He commands his troops into action.  The battle is joined.
The commander is dead.  On his body you find a map.

Congratulations.  You have completed your quest of eliminating the orc menace.  An orc and an orc child walk through the door.  "Raolph?  You made it!"  "Tugloc!  You found your son!"  Raolph and Tugloc embrace and slap each other on the back.

"My son was kidnapped by Commander Grunk and enslaved in this garrison.  Your attack on the Garrison headquarters gave me the chance to rescue him unnoticed.  For that I thank you.  I will now go back to my land and start anew, hoping to...

...convince my bretheren humans and orcs can live together and possibly even some day become allies and friends."  He shakes hands with Raolph and leaves, son by his side.  Raolph turns to you, "Let's get back to my village!  We have some celebrating..
...to do.
A sign on the door reads: "The guild is currently closed.  Come back later."

The townspeople come out to join you.  Among them is Raolph's wife....tears in her eyes.  Seeing Raolph is not with you she understands.  "I will miss my love, but he died saving our village and he will always be a hero."  Here is a token of our....
...appreciation.  She hands you your reward.

The townspeople come out to join you. Among them is Raolph's wife, tears of joy streaming down her face.  "You are all hero's!"  Raolph joins his wife and turns to you, "I'm not good at saying goodbye, but you all have a home here.  Here is a....
...small token of our appreciation.  He hands you your reward.
You gladly accept your reward and say your farewells.  You will long be remembered as the heroes who saved this small, seemingly insignificant village from certain death.  You move on.
As the map stated, the garrisons stash.
Congratulations.  You have completed your quest of eliminating the orc menace. You should get back to the village.  You have some celebrating to do.

A ladder stetches up to a trap door in the ceiling.  This room is empty except evidence exists which would lead you to beleive it has recently been occupied.  Pools of blood are in the corners and bits of bloodied bandages, broken weapons...
...and scraps of food are scattered about.

In this alcove lies a quite inebriated orc guard.  An empty bottle of wine lies next to him, its contents more on the floor and clothing then he could have possibly ingested.  Or could he?  He snores very loudly and is very unconcious.
You easily slit his throat.  He stops snoring.
Your searching reveals a key.
Impossible.  The snoring continues.
The door is locked.
The lock opens and the door stands ajar.
Your magic works to perfection.  The lock opens and the door stands ajar.
Some giant zombies erupt from 100-year-old crypts and attack on sight.
As you peruse the headstones, a gaggle of zombies unearth themselves and attack.
An incredible stench fills the air.  The odor of carrion, foul and strong, burns your nose as the gate swings open at your ever so slight touch.
Congratulations, you have eliminated the zombie menace from the graveyard.  A dark figure appears from nowhere and gives you your reward.
"Ahh....brave indeed.  Here is a map.  The reward is 500 gold plus anything you find in the graveyard.  Good luck."
A small hovel of a home sits deep in the sand.  A suprisingly old man emerges.  "Hello.  My name is Emi.  I have waited for you a long, long time.  Please, do come in."  Do you?

Upon entering the house you seem to feel as though it is much bigger on the inside than on the outside.  Even more strange is the fact that a stairs runs up the middle of what looked like a one story house up to the 2nd floor and beyond. Emi notices...

...your interest and wonderment. "Ahh.  A simple illusion.  I wouldn't have been able to stay secluded for so long to do my research if these simple , kind folk knew what I was up to.  Yes, there is a second, third, and fourth floor to my tower."  You ..

...surmise correctly he is of the magical persuasion.  "You are correct, I am trained in the arts of illusion and magic.  But enough about me.  I have brought you here for a reason.  The map you have in your memory was put there by me.  You see, I...

...am in need of your help.  A great evil is building a foothold in these parts and I have been charged by the mage masters to see to its snuffing out.  I cannot enlist the services of too powerful a party as it would draw undue attention to itself.  So..

...I summoned you to my aid.  You are a healthy lot of adventurers hungry for the thrill of money and power.  But, are you hungry for the thrill of justice and honor?  I hope so.  There are some things worth making right in this land of which this...

...is one.  Let me explain.  Throughout the years peace was supreme here.  All of the small villages you see now were together in one bright city called Flavin.  Flavin thrived for over 300 years.  Now, some eight years ago, flavin has split as...

...clouds of sand from who-knows-where descended upon the city, driving away its inhabitants and splintering Flavin into the small towns and villages dotting the land today.  The sand still remains now where  green lush land once stood.  There seems..

...to be a strange coincedence between the sand storms and the disappearance of two brothers, twins, Ollahn and Malear.  Of human descent, they vanished ten years ago and have never been heard of since.  I believe this to be of interest as...

...both of them were together when they vanished and the storms arrived in the exact location of their disappearance.  Now, we must find these twins and discover what connection they have to this scurge.  If we can discover the fate...

...which befell them we may have a chance to get to the root of this problem and restore the land to its original condition.  This is your mission.  Why should you accept this charge?  Simple.  Only I have the power to return you to...

...your homes far, far away from this place.  I will remain here as a source of information for you should you have any questions.  That is all I can tell you now.  If I uncover any information I will summon you.  Good luck."  With that, Emi...
...snaps his fingers and you find yourself outside his house, in a place unknown.
The door to the home is open, and no one seems to be around.  Do you enter?
A small home with a smoldering fireplace is unnattended.  Wait.  You notice a man asleep in a rocking chair near the fireplace, with a blanket over his lap.  He is snoring loudly.  What do you do?
He wakes with a start.  "Get out of here.  You can't just barge into someone's home and walk around like you own the place.  Get out, or I'll call the town guards!"  What do you do now?
After you knock, an old man comes to the door.  "Baahh.  Forgot to close my door, hey?  Thanks for letting me know.  Good day to you."  He shuts and locks the door.  Shortly you hear more snoring.
You allow the man to snore peacefully and leave.
A quick search reveals nothing.  The man stirs a bit, but then resumes snoring.
A second search reveals a trap door in the floor near the old man.  Will you open the door?
You back away from the trap door.
The trap door opens very quietly, and descends down into the depths.  Will you enter?
As you descend 10, 20, 30 feet the temperature cools.  You finally land some 40 feet below the surface of the old man's house and are in a 10x10 corridor pointing north.
Iron rungs lead up into the darkness.  Take them?
At the top of the stairs the old man is still sleeping.  You sneak out unnoticed.
You clumsy oafs have set off a trip wire.  Spears hurl at you from both sides of the walls.
You emerge near a group of shrubs on the other side of the mountains.
A nondescript piece of land revaels a secret door.  Do you open it?
As you descend 10, 20, 30 feet the temperature cools.  You finally land some 40 feet below the surface of the old man's house and are in a 10x10 corridor pointing south.
A lone troll was taking a break here....until he saw you.  He attacks.
A dead elf lies here, some of his items still in good condition.
A group of hell raisers are here waitin to pounce on some unsuspecting prey such as yourselves.  They attack.
Empty room.
In this corner a dying dwarf rests.  He looks up at you.  Death will soon take him.
Your effort proves fruitless.  The dwarf dies.

The dwarf shakes his head and gets up.  He is going to make it.  You have saved his life.  He speaks, "Thank you for saving me.  Damn troll almost got the best of me.  You could use someone like me.  I can swing an axe with the best of 'em.  My name is..
...Da'morc.  What say you?"  Do you want the dwarf to join you?
"I understand.  Thank you for saving me.  If we meet again I will be in your debt.  Farewell."  The dwarf trods off, no doubt to seek revenge on an ill-prepared troll.
"Very well.  I am honored to join you."  Da'morc gathers up his meager belongings and falls into rank.
A group of Ogres guard the pass.  They attack.
A man in a rickety old wagon drawn by a sorry looking horse pulls up to you.  Care to buy my wares?
A booming voice bellows, "What say you?"
"Return when you are ready."  You are thrown away from the lake.
"You are prepared.  Enter the home of Secja."  Huge rocks push up through the water.
A cleric approaches, "How may I help thee?"
A guard house hold 15 guards.  "I am sorry," says the captain, "you seem to have lost your way.  Please see the mayor.  Good day."  He sees you out.
What a sight.  Three goblins are taking on a young lad brandishing a lonsword and holding his own quite effectively.  Two other goblins lay dead next to the young man.  Do you help him out?
You join the fray.
Unfortunately, Rolian did not survive the battle.  You carry on.

Having destroyed the goblins Rolian approaches you.  "Excellent work, friends, but I must tell you I was doing fine on my own.  I appreciate the effort and bravery you have shown.  May I join you in search of adventure?
"Let us get going then.  I will inform the mayor.  This way."  He heads off to the south where you follow.
"I understand.  Enjoy your quests."  My heart and hopes go with you."  He gathers his belongings and moves on.

The mayor sits behind a large wooden (pine) desk.  He sees Rolian and stands up.  "Rolian, who are these strangers?"  Rolioan responds, "Mayor, there comes a time in everyone's life when certain decisions must be made.  I have come to ...

...one of those times.  I have decided to take on the challenge of adventure and move on with my new friends.  The village will be safe.  I will return."  The mayor looks at Rolian and nods slowly.  "Yes, Rolian, your time has come.  I have...

...something for your friends.  Use this wisely."  He opens up a small drawer in his desk and pulls out a ring.  "Use this in whichever way you see fit to keep Rolian in good health.  I must answer to his mother should injury befall him."  Rolian...

...turns to the mayor.  "Yes, mother.  Please tell her I love her and will be home again, safe and sound."  The mayor nods.  "It is settled then.  Take this gift and be off."  He tosses you the ring.  You grab it out of the air.
You gather your belongings and head out.
A young woman waves at you out of her small window.  After saying good day, she draws her blinds and says good night.
This completely undeveloped land hold terrible secrets.  One is revealed to you.
"Wait.  You carry the luck stone.  Please, follow us."  Do you follow?
"Fine.  Come back later, then.  Good day."
They form up in a most impressive formation and take you to see Allimac.

The men dismoount their horses and knock on the great Castle door.  The door silently opens.  One huge room is before you, with Queen Allimac on a throne at the opposite end.  She waves you all over.  The Captain of the guard speaks, "Allimac, Queen of...

...goodness and right, please forgive me.  I know you were not expecting...." "SILENCE!  What is the meaning of this intrusion,"  screams the Queen.  The Captain answers simply, "They carry the luck stone."  Allimac rises from her....

...throne.  "The luck stone?  So, you are the chosen ones.  Stories long ago told of a band of adventurers who carry the luck stone would bring our land back to peace.  I see you carry the stone.  You must be the party of the stories.  You have much...

...to do.  Here, sit.  You know the story of the twins.  Their disappearance has torn this land apart.  They must be re-joined.  I know where one of the twins is.  He is being held by Ja-Dran, a Red Dragon.  You must rescue him.  You cannot do this...

...without the Shield of the Eternal.  It will ease the pain of his greates asset;  He breathes fire.  I do not know where the Shield is, but I do know where Ja-Dran is.  Here is a map.  I can only help you this much, the rest is on your own.  Go now, ...
...take the map and hurry.  You will know what to do when you free the twin."  She gives you a map and the guards escort you to the border.

"Wait.  They have Ollahn with them, and he is alive!  Excellent work.  We will take him to safety.  I will infor the Queen of your success.  She will want to reward you.  She will be in touch."  Ollahn seems to know what is happening, and goes...
...with them.  You can only hope the Queen will keep him safe.
Ja-Dran was expecting you.  He leaps out of his lair and attacks with surprise.

The last breathe leaves Ja-Dran.  In his lair a young man is tied and gagged.  It is Ollahn!  Congratulations, you have found one of the twins.  Now, to get him back to the Queen.  Oh, yeah, there is some treasure in the Dragon's lair!
As if it was it's only goal, as Ja-Dran dies, the Shield of the Eternal changes into a normal shield.  Still magically enchanted, but no longer grants the wearer fire protection.
A booming voice calls out, "None shall pass who does not represent the Eternal."  You are forced back.

A group of wandering beasts smells you...they attack.
A small hut houses three women and a small girl.  They kindly ask you to leave.
A young man teaches his son the use of a dagger.  You hear him teach.  "The use of this will kill us some orc some day, sonny.  They will be coming for us soon."
A small, old man sells some leather goods.  Do you enter?
Som little girls are painting pictures of dead orcs on the side of the hut the reside in.  Very graphic indeed.
A bulking warrior lifts rocks and throws them a good 100 feet through the air.  He waves to you.  "Good day fine people.  I am Guntro.  I wait for the orcs.  Do you seek out the orcs?"

"Good.  Seek them out.  Kill them.  I will when they come.  They will come, you know.  You know that?  I knew you did.  You seek them out.  You kill them orcs."  He continues to throw rocks.  A very brainy endeavor.
"You don't seek them out.  Ah, you don't seek them out because you need more help.  I will help you.  Let's go.  Kill the orcs."  With that, you have a new member of your party.
An empty hut with a lot of rocks about 100 feet from it.
A small, empty hut.
A modest home holds a small group of orcs.  They see you, and sound an alarm.  More are sure to follow.
More orcs join the battle.
That should take care of most of the orcs around this village.
An empty home.
The house seems empty, but you hear a strange noise from inside the closed doors.  Care to investigate?
Inside the house you hear nothing.  Must have been your ears playing tricks on you.
You detect a secret room under the floor.  Want to open it?

In the small 10x10 room huddle a mother, father and 2 sons.  They squint as the light hits their eyes.  The father speaks, "Are the orcs gone?"  You tell them you have killed them all and they look relieved.  They come out of the hole.

The father continues, "Thank-you.  It was only a matter of time before they found us, too.  In order to repay you I have this.  My father told me when he dies it was important.  I don't know what it is.  Maybe you can tell me."  He hands you a...

...note.  It reads, "In times gone by only bravery survives.  In times gone by only truth survives.  In times gone by the sins go away.  In times gone by, gluttony never stays.  In times gone by, peace didn't survive.  Want to have peace?....

...Why?  Stop the sin with the Lizards color.  Be vocal against it and be on your way to peace, in times gone by."  The father thanks you and you move on, thinking this guy's father might just be nuts.
Nothing.
A few Orcs are still hanging out here.  They attack.
In the center of the room is a table upon the table lies an impressive sight.  A Shield.  Not just an ordinary shield.

Congratulations, you have secured the Shield of the Eternal.  No time for delaying, time for work.  As you turn to leave, a voice fills your head, "You have shown yourself worthy of the shield.  Now take on the responsibility and return peace."
A fire burns eternally here, with no way to put it out.  You find a store of rations here.
A small and unassuming hut houses some odd inhabitants.  They attack.
The remains of a family are here.  Slain are a mother, father, and two small girls.  The bodies are still warm.  The killers are in the area.
A man and his wife have been badly beaten.  The wife is already dead.  The father gurgles, "They headed south.... green, lizard like creatures.  Smell awful."  He dies.
A slain cleric lies here.  This used to be some sort of temple.  His body is still warm.
The sprawling village of Gunro lies before you.  Nice, clean homes line the busy streets.  Peolpe darting in and out of houses, laughing, playing, enjoying themselves.
A lovely home emaculately kept, as are most homes, lies quiet.
A dog has seen you through the window.  His bark alerts the owner.  A large woman wearing a blue blouse and skirt to match walks onto the step.  Don't mind Vic, he's harmless.  May I help you?
"Okay.  Have a good day."  The lady looks at you strangely and walks back into her home.  Vic doesn't let you out of his sight.
"The Temple?  It's right around the corner.  Just go up...oh, let me jot it down for you."  She quickly writes up a map to the city temple.
"The shop.  Just head East until you...  here, let me write up a map for you."  She scribes up and hands you a map.
"Ah, the Inn of Changing Winds.  Head East....here, I'll draw you a map."  She writes up a very detailed map and sends you on your way.
A temple.  Two clerics dressed in purple robes approach.  "How may we help thee?"
A lovely, slender woman waves you inside.  "My shop is always open.  Browse at your pleasure.....I mean leisure."
A large Inn with a bright red sign declares, "Inn of the Changing Winds."  Do you enter?
Would you like to leave the Inn?
The guard eyes you suspiciously, "Hey!  No entrance without a pass."  He shoos you away.

A rushed man lurches out of the house.  "It's about time you showed up.  I was told you would be here hours ago.  Here's my sword.  Have it fixed As soon as possible."  He tosses you a broken sword and shuts the door.
The man comes out of the house.  "You haven't fixed it yet?  Well, hurry up about it."  He slams the door.

The man emerges from his home.  "Ah.  It's fixed.  Fine work, too.  Here is the 2,000 gold we agreed upon.  Here.  My father always had this.  I know how you always talk about adventure.  Maybe this will be of help."  He hands you a ....
...piece of paper.  The paper reads, "If an adventure is what ye seek, seek the wandering man with the green rock."
The man emerges from his home.  "Hey!  Where is my sword?  Hurry up and get it back to me.  I've got things to do."  He slams the door.
A nondescript shop lies before you.  The shop owner approaches you.  "Please, enter if you like and shop.  I offer very reasonable prices."  He opens up the door and ushers you inside.
"Wait.  I see you have a broken sword.  I can fix it for you for 1,000 gold.  Would you like me to fix it?"

"Okay.  Just a minute."  He takes the sword and heads into a back room.  Three hours pass and all you hear is banging and clunking and an occasional yelp, but then he emerges with a bright, glistening piece of sword.
Sweat beading off his forhead, he pronounces, "All done.  Here you are."  He extends the sword but then pulls it back.  "Oh, almost forgot.  Who will be paying me the 1,000 gold?"
"Thank you.  I hope you enjoy the sword."  He hands it to you.
"Enjoy my shop."
"Don't have the money, huh?  I'll keep this until you do.  He slams the door."
"Back to pay?  Who will pay me the 1,000 you owe?"
You spot a  most loathful group of monsters.  They don't see you.  Attack?
An ugly old man is passed out drunk.  What do you do?
You carefully sidestep the drunk.  You hear a hickup, but nothing serious.

You shake the man and he comes into a state of semi-consciousness.  "M...m....mm.....my n, n,n, name isssss Du, Du, Dumin.  T, T, T, T, Ta, Ta, Take m, m, m, m, me to m, m, my r, r, ro, ro, roo, roo, room."  Wow, is he a mess.  You haven't...
...smelled anything like that since the  Dwarf in Bywater.  Do you help him?
You get him to his feet.  He mumbles something about the door to the east.  "Wait.  You'll n..n...nnn....need m...m...m...my p....paaa....paaassss.....ppppaaaasssssss."  He hands you his pass.
For a minute you thought you sensed something, but can't  get a fix on it.
You knew you sensed something.  A small cottage appears seemingly out of nowhere in the thick brush.
A patrol of orcs guards the fringe of camp.  They attack.
One of the Captains had a small stash on his person.

An ancient looking man in plate armor exits the home.  He looks up at you, "A keen sense you have, yes?  Not anyone has found me, no?  Now you have me, yes?  What do with me will you, yes?"  He stumbles off in a northern direction.
Do you follow?
The old man is here.  He taps on a tree four times and produces a piece of paper.  "This is what you seek.  Take it and listen for changing winds."  He hands you the paper.
You watch as the old man heads north and east and disappears into the woods.  I wonder where he went?
The guard eyes you suspiciously.  "I see you have a pass.  Enjoy the rest of the Inn."  He lets you through.
Do you want to leave this part of the Inn?
The guard passes you through the door.
You spot a group of orcs.  Attack them?
A hunched over little dwarf walks out of the hut.  He looks up at you, "What do you want?"

"Ah.  The trees.  My pride and joy.  No one could grow them as beautiful as I do.  Takes love and care, these trees.  They provide shade and refuge for weary travellers such as yourself.  But, as for the true power of the trees, you need to...

...do something for me.  I need special water from the southlands to water these trees, and my supply is running out.  Bring me some water to feed them with and I will realte to you the true power of the tree.  Will you?"
"Good.  I await your return."  He goes into his house and closes the door.
An unusual lake appears before you.  The color of the water is a little different from the rest of the streams and rivers you have encountered so far.
The canteen sinks into the lake.
The canteen then rises to the surface and levitates near you, full of the strange water which lies in this small lake.  Do you want to grab it?
You grab the container and secure it in your pack.
A group of strange bears have taken over this village.  They lumber out of the ravaged home and attack.
Some strange bear-like creatures inhabit this home.  They attack with extreme malice.
Some strange bear-like men inhabit this home.  They attack on sight.
An empty home.  Some ill-mannered beast has ravaged this place.  The floor boards seem a little squeaky, but the home is very old.
Your spell has discovered a secret area in the floor of the home.  Care to investigate?
You find a loose floorboard in the floor.  In it is a very ornate container, empty.
"Open sesame?!"  How weak.  Nothing happens.
"Who am I?  Who are you?"  He shuts the door.
"The traveling man?  He is a salesman who sells his junk to dumb people like you, if you buy it.  He wanders around an area to the north.  I have a map I could sell you for 100 gold?"
"Thank you."  He takes your gold and hands you a map.
"No gold?  No map."  He shuts the door.

"Time warp?  Yes, yes.  I do know of such a thing.  South of here, in a small alcove there is a strange man.  He controls time, so they say.  He may be able to help you.  I happen to have a map of the area if you are interested?  200 gold?"

"Ah.  You have the water.  Thank you.  Now, for the secret powers of the trees.  They are able to grant special protection to you as the ones who have watered them.  Take the water and use it on the trees.  The fifth tree from the west of....
...the northern row is the tree which controls the distribution of water to the other trees.  Place the container next to the tree and listen to the tree."  He closes the door.
An impressive tree, different from the others.  What do you do?
You place the container full of strange liquid next to the tree.  It sinks into the ground and disappears under the earth.

With a wrenching, painful noise, a mans face appears in the bark of the tree.  It speaks to you, "Good people, you have given us the strength to live on again for years to come.  As a payment to you, I guarantee your safety here for resting...

...and healing purposes.  No foul creature will harm you next to me.  You have given us life, and for that you shall recieve the opportunity to replenish yours."  The face recedes back into the tree and disappears.

"The ancient writ of Glopune?"  You are crazy.  Last report has a few dragons keeping it under cover in the nest they have.  Here's the last reported position, but...... anyway, it pays 2,000 gold.  Good luck, foolish adventurers."  He gives you a map.

In the sky you see what may be a small bird.  Lower and lower it descends, larger and larger a shadow it casts over you and your party.  A wrenching cry gives it away.  BLUE DRAGON!  Not one, but two!  They are on you with amazing quickness.
Having defeated the dragons, you see no sight of this Writ of Glopune!  It must be nearby.
Yes!  The lair of the blue dragons.  Inside the cave you discover a small blue dragon doing his best to guard the cave.  He attacks.
The baby Blue Dragon yelps one last time and falls dead.  Under his body lie some treasure.
Out of nowhere a dark robed figure appears with your reward.

"The lair of Bats?!?  No one has come back alive.  But you are the ones who are going to your deaths, not me.  Here's a map.  Good luck.  The pay is......, um, I guess you keep what you find."  He gives you a map.
The small town of Polin.  No one is out and about, strange for such a nice day.
You realize suddenly why no one is out and about.  A sound similar to rushing wind fills your ears.  You soon realize the sound is from bats.  Bats.  Bats.  Everywhere bats.  They attack.
With the attack over, you go about exploring this area.
The cave is currently empty.
What a sight.  Inside the cave are bats.  Lots and lots of bats.  They don't like intruders.  They attempt to remove you from this mortal coil.
Just when you think the fight is over, more bats attack.
The last of the bats falls.  You have completed this quest.  Down in the Guano, some treasure is hidden.  You unearth it.
"Sorry.  Someone else finished this quest.  I'll take it off the board."

"Wellton Parish has been feuding amongst itself for years.  If you can straighten things out, the surrounding traders have scraped up a 5,000 gold reward.  Good luck.  I don't have a map, but it lies due south of here."
The lovely Wellton Parish.  Well kept homes and streets highlight the town.  People are milling around and chatting happily.
The Wellton Parish.  People are milling about and speaking very friendly to each other.  A reverand comes up to you.  "How may we be of service."

You walk into the Wellton Parish.  You overhear some very harsh words being exchanged between two families.  "You know you stole it!  You know you did!"  The other family retorts, "We didn't, but your boy Smika did!"  The seemingly...

...happy Wellton Parish isn't so happy after all.  The two families look over their shoulders at you and return to the facade of happiness.  Then one father shakes his head, "We can't put up this facade any longer!  We have serious problems...
...and need someone to help us out!"  He turns to you.  "Can you help us get to the bottom of this?"
The father lowers his head.  "I understand.  Maybe it's better to work this out between ourselves."  They resume the facade of happiness and probably will never get to the bottom of the problem.

"Good.  Here is the problem.  They say we stole the golden orb, which has religious value to us.  We say the boy, Smika, took it.  Find out what happened and we will be grateful.  When you have the answer, come back here.  Thanks."

The families are gathered here.  You tell them the story about how neither one of them was at fault as a vampiric orc stole it under a spell making him look like Smika.  The two families take the Orb and place it on the mantle where...

...it belongs.  It glows and hums softly, and everyone in the room feels its peace.  The families thank you and embrace each other.  Smika's father speaks, "We know now the folly of blaming each other before knowing the full truth.  Maybe...

...next time we will work together with trust to find the truth."  The other father nods in agreement as the families head out the door together, speaking not under a facade of happiness, but in sincerity.  Congratulations, you have re-united...
...Wellton Parish.  A dark-robed figure appears from nowhere and gives you your reward.

The home of Smika, a six-year-old boy.  He approaches you, "No one believes me.  I didn't take the Orb.  I saw somebody who looked just like me around the Parish about 6 months ago.  It was wierd.  You believe me, don't you?"
A samll, 6-year-old boy plays in the dirt in fron of his house.  He pleasantly looks up at you and says hello.
His face brightens, "You do?!  You do!  Thanks."  I don't know where that person went who looks like me, but he went that way."  He points west.
Smika cries.  "No one will ever believe me.  I will always be blamed.  Always!"  He runs off to the east out of sight, his cries still audible.
Smika is here, playing in the dirt.  "Hi!  Found anything yet?  Okay.  See ya."  He returns to his playing.
Smika is here, singing and dancing.  "Hi!  Still looking, huh?  That's okay.  I know you will find out what happened."  He returns to his playing.
Smika is crying.  "You are the only ones who believe me.  Please hurry and find out what happened!  I can't take this!  Nobody likes me!"  He runs into the house crying.
A small shop.  The sign reads, "Closed until further notice."
A lovely lady sits on the porch in a rocking chair.  She greets you pleasantly and resumes her rocking.

A lady is rocking on the porch.  "You won't find who done it.  It was that Smika boy.  I saw him running out of the Parish bout 6 months back.  Next morning the Orb was gone.  Clean cut case a thiefin if ya ask me."  She goes back to rocking.
A lady is rocking on the porch.  "That Smika boy took the orb, ya know.  I seen him runnin out the Parish six months back.  Stole it, he did.  Stole it and sold it."  She goes back to rocking.

A lady is rocking on the porch.  She gets up and yells at you, "You oughta put that Smika boy in the jail where he belongs!  I saw him runnin out the Parish six months back.  Next mornin' Orb was G-O-N-E, gone!"  She resumes her rocking.
A young man polishes a sword.  "Hi!  Have a good day!"  He returns to his polishing.
A young man looks at you.  "Why are you helping us?  You should mind your own business."
The man looks flustered.  "I, I don't know anything about it!  Leave me alone!"  He is breaking a sweat.
"Good.  We can handle this ourselves."  He looks more relaxed as he goes back in his house.
"Oh yeah.  Well, I don't know anything.  Just leave us alone!"  He is really sweating.  He looks like he might have a coronary at any moment.
"Okay.  Wee, okay then.  Have a nice afternoon."  He goes into his house.
"You challenge me!  If you are going to be that bold, it will be a duel.  Do you accept, coward?"
"I thought not.  Now begone coward, and bug me no more."

The boy enters your room.  "5 gold please!  Who will be paying?"

All of your equipment is safe and sound here.  Do you want to remove your brown court robes and take back your equipment?

Side with the Guards!
Side with Ponburk!

You jump to the side of Ponburk and his men, who are indeed in need of your help.  The battle is joined.

"I understand.  It would be difficult, and I'm sure you have better things to do.  Good luck to you.  I will have to manage this one on my own."  Ponburk sees you out.

Ponburk sees you coming and quickly ushers you inside.    He reads the letter from the orc commander and sees it addressed to Kolarin.  "This is the evidence we needed.  Let's be off to see the mayor."  Ponburk gathers his things and joins you.

"Seems like the orcs and goblins are working to take over this land.  Most of the outlying areas are already wiped out or are darn close to it.  Rumor has it the Queen has been looking very hard for the twins because she is trying to save them."

"I remember hearing of a huge metalic creature which shoots fire from its mouth.  I also heard there is some magical tube which is the only way to take it out.  Speaking of magic, I heard Queen Allimac is looking for some green rock."

"Some fool told me the Captain of the Ruwarian guard is in cahoots with the orcs.  I've known Kolarin for years.  No way he is in cahoots with anyone except a few ladies......har, har , arrgh...  He's looking for a green rock a man in the woods sells."
"Prince Corin has his men out looking for the twins.  He'll find them soon enough.  Seems that's the only way to get rid of these orcs, is to re-unite the twins."

The oldest drunk man greets you at the door.  "Care to come in for a drink?

Care for another drink?
